questions.prompt: What can Anton directly infer from the original attendance record?
options: Few people attended at that offered time, while their motives are not recorded by the list.
Every registered person has lost interest because the class has too little variety.
Every absence is explained by shift work, as Romy's own schedule demonstrates.
questions.explanation: Attendance is observed; motivation and causes require further evidence. Romy explicitly refuses to explain every absent person through her own experience.
evidence: „Zuerst nur, dass wenige Menschen um diese Uhrzeit hier waren“
Sie wollte weder für sämtliche Abwesenden sprechen noch jedes versäumte Training automatisch mit Arbeit erklären.

questions.prompt: What does the alternating-time trial actually provide?
options: One existing weekly hour rotates between confirmed rooms and paid times on an early published plan.
Two weekly classes replace the original hour, with the additional time covered by Anton’s existing unpaid preparation.
A rotating weekly time is chosen from members’ messages shortly before each session.
questions.explanation: Capacity is rearranged, not expanded without resources. The six-week timetable makes actual dates, hours and rooms knowable in advance.
evidence: Die Zahl der angebotenen Wochenstunden würde dadurch gleich bleiben.
mit Datum, Uhrzeit und Raum.

questions.prompt: Why does Anton prepare independent units with an introduction at each meeting?
options: The independent units let him omit introductions for returning members who have missed a week.
Missing one week must not make the next session unusable through unexplained continuity.
Rotating the schedule is enough to maintain access to his existing continuous sequence.
questions.explanation: A rotated schedule can still exclude people if content depends on the skipped session. Anton adapts the actual learning sequence as well as the clock time.
evidence: damit das Fehlen in einer Woche die nächste Teilnahme nicht unbrauchbar machte.
Er plante für den Versuch eigenständige Einheiten mit einer Einführung bei jedem Termin.

questions.prompt: What does Mina's continuing dissatisfaction show about the revised service?
options: Its attendance figures prove that every member has benefited equally.
It preserves the original regular access while adding two usable trial appointments for Mina.
It improves access for some while removing a reliably useful old slot for another participant.
questions.explanation: Mina loses a familiar workable time and can use only two trial dates. Her loss remains part of the evaluation alongside newly enabled attendance.
evidence: „Mein fester Termin geht dabei verloren“
Mina blieb mit der Unregelmäßigkeit unzufrieden.

questions.prompt: How does the six-response enquiry limit the explanation of original nonattendance?
options: It gives a complete reason for every registered member's absence.
It identifies several different barriers while leaving the reasons of nonresponders unknown.
It shows that any member preferring a different hour was never genuinely interested.
questions.explanation: Work, care and preference appear in the received replies. Unanswered questionnaires do not establish another category of motive.
evidence: Vier beschrieben Arbeitszeiten
Die übrigen Angemeldeten hatten nicht geantwortet, sodass deren Gründe unbekannt blieben.

questions.prompt: Why does Romy qualify Anton's claim about the second attendance list too?
options: She now agrees attendance is a complete substitute for asking about needs.
She thinks the trial should count every possible appointment as actual participation.
Even better access does not let attendance figures fully measure her motivation or private decisions.
questions.explanation: Romy attends twice but chooses not to use another possible date. The trial improves real opportunities without making the new list a complete psychological measure.
evidence: „Und die zweite kennt sie auch nicht vollständig“
hatte einen anderen möglichen Termin aus privaten Gründen nicht genutzt.

review.notes: Direct German/six-item audit. Checked attendance versus motive, six response limits, confirmed one-hour rotation, self-contained content need, Mina loss and second-list limits.

peerReview.notes: Full-source independent review of all question fields. Strengthened irrelevant/absolute alternatives with same-plot misunderstandings about incentives, budgets, rotating units, display timing and the bounded quieter course. Confirmed that individual reports do not support universal judgements.

questions.prompt: Why does moving away from the speaker and reducing the music not resolve Nadja's first difficulty?
options: The adjustments make her follow the sequence but do not preserve the friends’ shared journey home.
Several competing sounds remain hard for her to separate, beyond the speaker's distance alone.
The visible display remains blocked from her new position during Mika’s demonstrations.
questions.explanation: The alternative room has not yet been prepared. Her report concerns simultaneous sound sources, and the first adjustments do not adequately change that.
evidence: Eine bloß leiser gestellte Musik beseitigte für sie nicht die Schwierigkeit mehrerer gleichzeitig laufender Geräusche.

questions.prompt: What work is needed beyond switching the music off?
options: A usable visible sequence, checked sight lines, an appropriate room and actual paid coaching time.
The same microphone sequence can be reused with no further room or teaching changes.
A display alone can replace all spoken explanation once each participant has learned its colours.
questions.explanation: The quiet option is its own prepared course. Mika tests the room and corrects a blocked display before relying on it.
evidence: eine vorbereitete Anzeige und tatsächliche Betreuungszeit.
Er verschob seinen Vorführplatz und prüfte die Sicht erneut.

questions.prompt: What does Lena's participation in the second quiet trial establish?
options: Understanding Nadja's needs makes Lena obliged to stay in that course permanently.
The quiet option is automatically the best solution for both friends.
She can understand its benefit for Nadja while still preferring the rhythmic Thursday session herself.
questions.explanation: Lena tries it, follows it with more effort and finds it less stimulating. Nadja does not demand a shared preference in return for the effort.
evidence: „Ich verstehe jetzt besser, was dir hilft, aber ich möchte hier nicht bleiben“

questions.prompt: What remains unresolved after Nadja can use the quieter course?
options: A dependable replacement for the friends' shared evening and journey.
Whether Farah has approved paid coaching for any of the four quieter trials.
Whether Lena will try the quieter option before deciding which course to attend.
questions.explanation: The access improvement separates their course days. They intend to compare calendars, but have not established a regular shared alternative.
evidence: Die technische Lösung im Raum hatte die Freundschaftsplanung nicht gleich mitgelöst.
ein verlässlicher neuer gemeinsamer Abend fehlte ihnen noch.

questions.prompt: Why does Mika avoid deciding which friend's perception of the original course is correct?
options: Lena's use of rhythm proves Nadja should continue until she adjusts.
Nadja's report proves rhythmic guidance never provides useful orientation to anyone.
The same sound arrangement supports one person and hinders another, requiring different workable access rather than a winner.
questions.explanation: Lena relies on rhythm and Nadja struggles with competing sounds. Recognising both explains why an alternative needs different guidance instead of invalidating either account.
evidence: die rhythmischen Hinweise ihr selbst Orientierung gaben.
„Wir müssen nicht entscheiden, wessen Wahrnehmung die richtige ist“

questions.prompt: What can be claimed about the quieter course's future after four trials?
options: It is guaranteed permanently for every week of the next calendar year.
A further limited period has confirmed staffing, while a permanent annual schedule remains undecided.
The original four-session budget covers the entire next year because the room remains available.
questions.explanation: Farah and Mika examine use and work before confirming the next bounded period. Continued operation is specific, not a perpetual promise.
evidence: für einen weiteren begrenzten Zeitraum mit bestätigter Betreuung angeboten.
Ein dauerhafter Stundenplan für das ganze nächste Jahr war damit noch nicht beschlossen.

review.notes: Direct source/all-item audit. Checked first adjustment before later display, different valid perceptual needs, real paid alternative design, temporary continuation and remaining friendship/time loss.

peerReview.notes: Full-source independent review of all question fields. Strengthened irrelevant/absolute alternatives with same-plot misunderstandings about incentives, budgets, rotating units, display timing and the bounded quieter course. Confirmed that individual reports do not support universal judgements.

questions.prompt: What help did the narrator originally request from Oskar?
options: Permanent public commentary on any picture connected with health or food.
Reminders about their shared appointments, not general judgement of meals and all other time.
A weekly duty to approve every private plan outside their Tuesday meeting.
questions.explanation: The initial shared schedule and limited campaign do not establish a general supervisory role. The narrator acknowledges requesting help without accepting its expansion.
evidence: Ich hatte um Erinnerung an gemeinsame Termine gebeten, nicht um Bewertungen meiner Mahlzeiten und jeder freien Stunde.

questions.prompt: Why is ending the automatic data share only part of the solution?
options: It ends the access that had originally given Oskar permission to comment publicly on meals.
It removes one information source but not the habit of turning other available details into judgements.
It retrospectively deletes the birthday comment from every reader's experience.
questions.explanation: Oskar can still see pictures and remarks. The boundary concerns what role he assumes from access, not only which data channel remains open.
evidence: Damit verschwand eine Informationsquelle, nicht automatisch seine Angewohnheit, aus Bildern und Bemerkungen neue Urteile abzuleiten.

questions.prompt: How does Oskar's account of his own need for accountability affect the assessment of his behaviour?
options: It proves the public birthday comment was a necessary form of support.
It shows the original request for help already included the style of accountability he needs himself.
It explains part of his projection without supplying consent or excusing the public remark.
questions.explanation: Oskar recognises he transferred his preferred form of commitment. He then corrects the remark in the same group, but explanation does not cancel its effect.
evidence: „Ich habe meine Art von Verbindlichkeit einfach zu deiner gemacht“
Das erklärte etwas, entschuldigte aber den öffentlichen Kommentar nicht.

questions.prompt: What does the later conversation about the garden show?
options: Trust has returned fully because any mention of a photograph is now harmless.
Oskar is again checking the narrator's food by asking about the broken sunshade.
Ordinary friendship talk is possible while the narrator's initial tension still reflects the earlier experience.
questions.explanation: The narrator tenses before hearing the actual question, then can discuss the garden. Improvement does not mean immediate complete ease.
evidence: Ich wurde sofort angespannt, bevor ich wusste, welche Frage folgen würde.
nicht sofort wieder dieselbe Unbefangenheit herstellte.

questions.prompt: Why is the narrator's later request to move Tuesday a different use of Oskar's support?
options: It concerns a defined shared decision on which his availability is relevant.
It gives him authority to examine the rest of the week before agreeing.
It reactivates the old automatic attendance report as a necessary condition.
questions.explanation: The narrator asks a concrete question about a mutual appointment. Oskar checks his calendar and agrees without requiring unrelated private information.
evidence: „Kannst du dann noch gemeinsam trainieren?“
ohne nach den übrigen Tagen meiner Woche zu fragen.

questions.prompt: Why does Oskar correct his birthday remark in the original message group?
options: The inappropriate public statement needs clarification for the audience that saw it, while the unpleasant moment cannot be undone.
A private clarification would let the group infer that the original food comment was still justified.
The public correction clarifies the narrator’s meal choices by explaining how they fit the training plan.
questions.explanation: Oskar states the food was not his business to judge. The cousin welcomes this, but the original experience remains part of why the narrator is cautious.
evidence: Oskar schrieb später in dieselbe Geburtstagsgruppe
der unangenehme Moment war damit trotzdem nicht rückwirkend verschwunden.

review.notes: Full German/direct six-question audit; unnamed narrator preserved (old Luisa unsupported). Checked initial limited request, active old data share, access versus authority, same-audience correction, defined later help and residual tension.

peerReview.notes: Independent complete-source and question-field audit. Strengthened same-plot distractors about limited support/data access, equipment compatibility, public correction and sponsorship conditions. Checked exact budget, dissent, Ben’s actual participation and the continuing trust effects.

questions.prompt: Why do Hanna and Noah read the unattended towel differently?
options: Noah sees a pause in continuing use, while Hanna cannot distinguish that from an item left behind.
The sign explicitly says that all towels reserve equipment for the entire afternoon.
Hanna knows the towel belongs to Noah but assumes his exercise has formally ended.
questions.explanation: The local signal and written sign do not explain pauses. Marta treats the disagreement as an unclarified expectation rather than proof of deliberate discourtesy.
evidence: Von Pausen zwischen zusammengehörigen Trainingsabschnitten stand dort nichts.
Noah hatte sein Handtuch nicht als aufgegebenen Gegenstand verstanden; Hanna hatte keinen laufenden Gebrauch erkennen können.

questions.prompt: Why can these two participants alternate at the first bench?
options: The shared bench allows Hanna to use Noah’s weights while he takes his planned pause.
Noah agrees to eliminate all his planned rest periods so Hanna can proceed.
Their checked tasks use the same backrest setting and separate weights.
questions.explanation: Marta checks their actual plans. Compatibility makes this solution workable without altering Noah's needed pause or inviting changes to his equipment without asking.
evidence: Beide benötigten für ihre bereits eingeführten Aufgaben dieselbe Einstellung der Lehne und getrennte eigene Hanteln.

questions.prompt: Why is a different solution agreed at the later station?
options: The tasks need reconfiguration, making a clear sequence more suitable than alternating.
The tasks use different equipment settings, so the participants must shorten each other’s pauses.
The later station falls under the old sign, so ongoing use during a pause is no longer allowed.
questions.explanation: A useful communication method does not imply the same equipment arrangement everywhere. Marta refuses to turn a successful local workaround into a universal duty.
evidence: Dort passten die vorgesehenen Aufgaben nicht ohne Umbau zusammen
Marta wollte das Abwechseln nicht zur Pflicht machen

questions.prompt: What changes in Noah's interaction with the next new member?
options: He announces the bench is abandoned even though his training is continuing.
He states his continuing use and asks about the newcomer's plan rather than relying on the towel alone.
He lets the towel guarantee an indefinite reservation without personal contact.
questions.explanation: The equipment may look momentarily empty, but its next use is now explained aloud. The newcomer can ask and negotiate rather than guess.
evidence: „Ich benutze die Bank noch; was hast du vor?“
die nächste Nutzung wurde gerade laut besprochen.

questions.prompt: What does Noah acknowledge about his phone break without giving up the need for a pause?
options: Using a phone means he never had any claim to finish the planned exercise.
The message took longer than expected and he could have explained the ongoing use earlier.
His own sense of an obvious towel rule obliges Hanna to know his whole sequence.
questions.explanation: Noah's rest between sections is a real part of his plan, but this does not make unexplained waiting by others automatically acceptable.
evidence: „Aber ich habe die Nachricht länger beantwortet, als ich vorher gedacht hatte“
„Nächstes Mal sage ich früher Bescheid“

questions.prompt: Why does Hanna find the conflicting confident advice from other members unhelpful?
options: It proves there are no circumstances where equipment can remain in use during a pause.
Their disagreement is about whose training matters more, while the written rule already explains pauses.
Each treats a different assumption as obvious, without resolving the missing information about present use.
questions.explanation: One member treats a towel as reservation; another points out indefinite blocking. The certainty of the statements does not make the incomplete local rule clearer.
evidence: „Offenbar kennen hier mehrere Menschen unterschiedliche offensichtliche Regeln“

review.notes: Direct source/six-item audit. Checked unattended versus paused use, incomplete sign, Noah's real rest plus overlong call, trainer-checked compatibility and station-specific alternatives without exercise advice.

peerReview.notes: Independent complete-source and question-field audit. Strengthened same-plot distractors about limited support/data access, equipment compatibility, public correction and sponsorship conditions. Checked exact budget, dissent, Ben’s actual participation and the continuing trust effects.

questions.prompt: What condition does Armin explicitly attach to his additional support?
options: The club must promise Ben some playing time later, without guaranteeing a place in the starting line-up.
The club must give the business visible thanks while Jonas remains free to choose the starting team.
His son Ben must have a starting position in the next game.
questions.explanation: Lena clarifies the implication directly, and Armin expressly confirms money depends on the starting place.
evidence: „Von einem Platz in der ersten Aufstellung, ja“

questions.prompt: Why does Ben starting for legitimate sporting reasons not remove the funding issue?
options: The financial condition would still become an added criterion and future expectation.
A sporting start would require treating the payment as confirmed income before the board considers it.
The payment would still replace the club’s confirmed regular budget rather than funding the proposed additions.
questions.explanation: Coinciding once with the normal selection does not make a conditional payment independent. It changes the explanation and pressure on later choices.
evidence: „Dann hätten wir diese Aufstellung und eine Erwartung für die nächste“
Ein zusätzlicher finanzieller Grund würde diese Erklärung verändern

questions.prompt: What concrete financial loss does the board accept?
options: All regular hall and travel spending is cancelled while the 1,500 euros remains available.
The confirmed budget remains 2,500 euros, with new uniforms and the extra outing dropped.
Other unconfirmed shop contacts automatically replace the declined amount.
questions.explanation: The additional 1,500 would fund 500-euro uniforms and a 1,000-euro trip. Rejection leaves existing regular activities funded but real additions lost.
evidence: Das Zusatzgeld soll neue Trikots für fünfhundert Euro und einen Trainingsausflug für tausend finanzieren.
Neue Trikots werden nicht bestellt, und der geplante zusätzliche Trainingsausflug entfällt.

questions.prompt: How does Jonas treat Ben after the offer is refused?
options: He retains the same sporting criteria without rewarding or punishing the child for his father's condition.
He guarantees Ben future starts to reassure him after rejecting the money.
He keeps Ben out of the next game to show the board that rejecting the offer has no exceptions.
questions.explanation: Ben is not responsible for Armin's decision. He starts on the bench and later plays according to the actual coaching choice, without a permanent guarantee.
evidence: „Du wirst weder für Geld bevorzugt noch wegen dieser Sache bestraft“

questions.prompt: What does Lena acknowledge when families are disappointed by the cancelled outing?
options: They should have known no proposal is ever worth planning around.
The lost outing can be replaced once either of the two possible shop contacts replies.
She made a tentative opportunity sound too certain before income was confirmed.
questions.explanation: Lena owns the communication problem and explains missing funds without blaming Ben. She offers no immediate replacement based on merely possible sponsors.
evidence: Lena übernimmt die Verantwortung dafür, dass die Möglichkeit zu früh zu sicher geklungen hat.
Ein sofortiges Ersatzversprechen gibt sie nicht

questions.prompt: Which detail limits a reading of the board's decision as a unanimous resolution of the conflict?
options: All five board members support refusal once the trip's cost becomes clear.
Three members support refusal and two prefer another solution; real disappointment continues.
The team's loss proves the lower budget was the cause of its performance.
questions.explanation: The decision is authorised but contested. The story preserves both recorded dissent and disappointment about the lost trip, without turning a narrow loss into budget proof.
evidence: Drei der fünf zuständigen Mitglieder haben für die Ablehnung gestimmt, zwei hätten eine andere Lösung bevorzugt.
„Der Ausflug wäre trotzdem schön gewesen“

review.notes: Full source/six-item audit. Checked explicit conditional start, future pressure despite coincidence, 2500/1500/500/1000 budget, majority not unanimity, no child blame or punishment and no causal claim from match loss.

peerReview.notes: Independent complete-source and question-field audit. Strengthened same-plot distractors about limited support/data access, equipment compatibility, public correction and sponsorship conditions. Checked exact budget, dissent, Ben’s actual participation and the continuing trust effects.

questions.prompt: Why do the same two practice hits receive different totals before the event?
options: One club has already entered official final-round results while the other is practising.
The clubs use distinct local scoring variants that were never agreed as one tournament system.
One club counts the adapted starting positions as extra points while the other counts only hits.
questions.explanation: One system counts each hit equally and the other awards more for the centre. Familiar equipment does not establish shared rules.
evidence: Es handelte sich um zwei lokale Varianten, nicht um ein gemeinsam vereinbartes Turnierregelwerk.

questions.prompt: Why would imposing the host club's score system now not fully repair the competition?
options: Using the host system would erase the guests’ preparation because their earlier practice results would have to be deleted.
The differing preparations would become comparable once both practice totals were converted into one scale.
A clear number cannot retrospectively equalise preparation or settle unagreed positions and aids.
questions.explanation: The clubs prepared for different strategies. Conditions also include more than scoring; agreeing after arrival cannot create prior shared preparation.
evidence: die unterschiedliche Vorbereitung nicht nachträglich vergleichbar gemacht.
Die unterschiedlichen Ausgangspositionen und Hilfen mussten dabei ebenso geklärt werden wie die Punkte.

questions.prompt: What is Tim able to choose under the specific replacement offer?
options: He must stay because paying the fee made every later format binding.
He takes the offered participation-fee refund and leaves rather than accept the exercise format.
He receives all travel costs automatically regardless of his decision.
questions.explanation: The organisers offer a real exit for this change. Tim's reasons remain valid even though the narrator prefers to stay; travel expenses are separate.
evidence: Die bereits entstandenen Fahrtkosten wurden dadurch nicht automatisch erstattet.
Tim aus unserer Gruppe entschied sich, die Rückzahlung anzunehmen und früher abzureisen.

questions.prompt: How are the results of the joint practice stations treated?
options: As evidence for a common system already confirmed by both clubs before their next meeting.
As evidence that the host variant is the only correct version of the sport.
As explained local exercise results, without merging them into a tournament ranking.
questions.explanation: Participants learn both variants with explained conditions. A future common rule text and event remain work to do rather than something the exercise scores settle.
evidence: Diese Übungsergebnisse sollten ausdrücklich nicht zu einer gemeinsamen Rangliste zusammengerechnet werden.

questions.prompt: What does David recognise after Rike responds to his suggestion that the guests should have asked?
options: His answer about usual club rules assumed his own familiar system without specifying it for both groups.
The guests had received a complete rule book but chose not to read it.
The guest club had asked about materials but never asked which rules would govern the event.
questions.explanation: Rike had asked and was given the same vague wording. David owns the missing shared agreement rather than treating the guests' reliance on the reply as the cause.
evidence: „Wir hatten nach den üblichen Regeln gefragt und genau diesen Satz bekommen“
räumte ein, nur an die Regeln seines eigenen Clubs gedacht zu haben.

questions.prompt: Why does the narrator say both that learning occurred and that the advertised tournament did not happen?
options: The substitute can have real value without erasing the lost purpose and unheld competition.
The exercises are valueless unless everyone remains to compete for the original trophy.
The successful stations retroactively fulfil every expectation that brought Tim to the event.
questions.explanation: The narrator resists reducing the account to success alone. The trophy is put away and the ranking remains an open future task.
evidence: „Ich habe etwas gelernt, aber das angekündigte Turnier hat nicht stattgefunden“
Den Pokal brachte er nicht als Trostpreis zu unserer Gruppe

review.notes: Direct source/all-item audit. Checked two local variants, no rated round begun, preparation and aid rules, specific refund/travel limit, voluntary substitute and learning without retroactive tournament fulfilment.

peerReview.notes: Complete German source and all quiz fields independently reviewed. Strengthened distractions into documented near misses about score conversion, missed handover timing, protected reservations and water-source capacity. Verified scope of refunds, actual report correction, conditional limits and future uncertainty.

questions.prompt: Why do Aylin, Mira and Karl miss their own race?
options: They freely choose in advance to exchange every chance to race for a full-day volunteering role.
They first report the missing handover after all runners have finished.
The promised relief lacks a confirmed person and arrives only after their start window has closed.
questions.explanation: Their saved message predates the planned change. The organisational gap, not late reporting, prevents the promised combination of service and racing.
evidence: Als die tatsächliche Übergabe möglich wurde, war der Start ihres angemeldeten Laufs bereits vorbei.
Sie hatten die fehlende Ablösung bereits vor dem vorgesehenen Wechsel gemeldet.

questions.prompt: What does Felix correct in the club report?
options: The three participants’ help is recorded as replacing the need to document their missed start.
The account that the three voluntarily gave up their start, while retaining recognition of their help.
The missing relief is recorded as a last-minute change reported only after the planned handover.
questions.explanation: Agreeing to temporary help was not consent to lose participation. Correcting that distinction does not require denying their contribution.
evidence: Ihre Unterstützung blieb anerkannt, die vermeintliche freie Entscheidung zum Nichtstart dagegen nicht.

questions.prompt: What makes the next race reservations more concrete than the first promise?
options: The three are again the unnamed backup for every gap before their own start.
The same vague hope of a later relief is repeated with more appreciative wording.
Protected participant places are backed by other confirmed trained staff, a reserve and funded additional help.
questions.explanation: The plan assigns and pays for real capacity, losing part of the closing event in exchange. The same people are not silently used to fill the missing shift again.
evidence: ein geplanter Teil der Abschlussfeier weg.
Es gab außerdem eine benannte Reserve für die betreffenden Dienste.

questions.prompt: What remains unrecovered for Aylin despite accepting the new opportunity?
options: The future reservation requires her to agree to any date without checking her work.
The missed original race and its shared experience with Noah cannot be recreated by a later separate start.
The protected reservation guarantees that the future race will reproduce her expected original result.
questions.explanation: Aylin checks the date and chooses a new chance. Noah cannot run then, and the future event has not yet happened, so it is not a retroactive replacement.
evidence: Noah konnte am nächsten Datum nicht mitlaufen
nicht als schon geschehenen Ersatz für ihr verlorenes Ergebnis.

questions.prompt: How does Felix revise his first explanation after Karl shows the saved message?
options: He recognises that blaming their warning time shifted an already-reported gap onto the helpers.

questions.prompt: Which part of the published criticism requires a factual correction?
options: The attribution to the director needs correction, while the description of Faris’s independent timing remains valid.
The reported effect on the critic needs correction, while the attribution to Faris remains a reasonable inference from the performance.
The claim that Faris independently chose the long pauses, rather than the critic’s negative experience of them.
questions.explanation: The pauses and the critic’s response are real observations. The unsupported, checkable assertion is that the actor introduced the rhythm on his own, which the later rehearsal evidence contradicts.
evidence: eine unüberprüfte Behauptung über den Urheber
Die Kritik beschrieb zwar meinen wirklichen Eindruck

questions.prompt: How is the responsibility for the rhythm established rather than merely reassigned after a complaint?
options: Mara describes her general intention, and the editor infers from that account that she must also have prescribed these pauses.
Dated rehearsal instructions identify Mara’s direction, and she confirms it directly to the editorial team.
Faris supplies dated instructions, but their link to this monolog remains unconfirmed when the revised attribution is published.
questions.explanation: Karim does not treat a general complaint as sufficient proof. The team checks instructions tied to the specific monolog and obtains direct confirmation of the directing decision.
evidence: die betreffenden datierten Probenhinweise
Mara bestätigte die Entscheidung anschließend direkt gegenüber der Redaktion.

questions.prompt: Why does learning Mara’s intention not oblige the critic to find the monolog convincing?
options: The critic accepts the intended distance as successful but still rejects Faris’s way of carrying out the documented instruction.
The critic separates the actor’s choices from the director’s but reserves the earlier factual attribution until another performance is seen.
Understanding the source of a choice is distinct from experiencing its intended artistic effect.
questions.explanation: The critic can now attribute the choice accurately while still describing the distance as unsuccessful. Both Karim and Faris distinguish correcting authorship of the action from demanding an agreeable review.
evidence: musste aber weder ihre beabsichtigte Wirkung als meine eigene Erfahrung übernehmen
die Wirkung auf mich beschreibe ich trotzdem nach meinem tatsächlichen Besuch

questions.prompt: Why are both the original article and its short preview changed?
options: The article’s attribution changes, while the preview is changed to explain why the critic now accepts Mara’s intended effect.
Both conveyed the false attribution, and the visible correction must be connected with the original criticism.
The preview carries the correction notice, while the original article retains its earlier wording as a record of the first impression.
questions.explanation: The preview had highlighted the supposedly self-chosen pauses. Correcting it as well as the article prevents the false attribution from remaining a current summary, while a clear notice makes the change traceable.
evidence: Die Änderung muss bei der ursprünglichen Kritik auffindbar sein
Die kurze Vorschau des Artikels wurde ebenfalls berichtigt

questions.prompt: What has the reader misunderstood when she says the criticism was withdrawn under pressure?
options: The critic has corrected who chose the pauses but still judges the scene negatively.
The correction withdraws criticism of Faris’s interpretation but leaves a negative judgment of the director’s intended effect.
The correction changes the reported audience reaction rather than the critic’s account of responsibility for the scene.
questions.explanation: The revised article still contains a negative evaluation. The critic points out that changing an incorrect claim about the scene’s creation is not equivalent to changing the reported effect of watching it.
evidence: die weiterhin negative Beschreibung der Szene
ich habe die Verantwortung dafür zuvor dem falschen Menschen zugeschrieben

Das machte meine Wahrnehmung nicht automatisch genauer in jeder Frage
